Interface RmiClientService

All Superinterfaces:
Remote
All Known Implementing Classes:
VirtualServerRMI
public interface RmiClientService extends Remote
Remote callback exposed by the client and called by the server in the RMI transport.

The RMI client has two directions:

  • client to server: RmiServerService, used by the client to send commands;
  • server to client: RmiClientService, used by the server to push updates back.

The concrete client-side implementation is VirtualServerRMI. The name is intentional in the project architecture: from the client point of view it behaves like a local "virtual server" that receives messages coming from the real server and routes them to the UI.

This interface is placed in the shared package because Java RMI requires both JVMs to know the same remote type. The server receives an implementation of this interface during connection setup and stores it inside the per-client RMI session.

  • Method Details

    • handleMessage

      void handleMessage(ServerMessage message) throws RemoteException
      Receives one application message from the server.

      Server-side code calls this method when it wants to notify the client about lobby updates, lobby lists, game updates, or application errors. The client implementation routes the message to the local ClientView through the client-side message router.

      Parameters:
      message - server-to-client message containing a type and its payload
      Throws:
      RemoteException - if the callback cannot be delivered to the client JVM

    • handlePing

      void handlePing() throws RemoteException
      Receives a keep-alive PING from the server.

      The client implementation answers by asking ServerProxyRMI to call RmiServerService.pong(it.polimi.ingsoft.mesos.shared.payload.clienttoserver.connection.PongPayload) on the remote server session.

      Throws:
      RemoteException - if the callback cannot be delivered to the client JVM
